You are given the transcription of one page of a historical German document, one line per entry, each line prefixed with its id (l1, l2, …). The transcription is diplomatic: old spelling, ſ (long s), abbreviations and line-end hyphens are as the page has them. Translate it into English, sentence by sentence.

- One segment per sentence of the source. A sentence may run over several lines; a segment then names its first and last line id. A segment must never skip a line that lies between its first and last line.
- Translate in order, and cover every line that holds text. A line that is only a page number, a catchword or an ornament still gets a segment, translated as it stands (a number stays a number).
- Keep the source's gaps and doubts: where the German has [...] write [...] in the English; where it has [?word] translate the word and keep the marker, as [?word].
- Do not resolve abbreviations, fill gaps, correct the German, or modernise names. Translate what is there.
- Where a line-end hyphen splits a word across two lines, translate the whole word once.
- "first_words" and "last_words" are the first three and the last three words of the source sentence, copied verbatim from the transcription (with ſ, if the transcription has it).
- "note" is for a genuine difficulty with the German (an ambiguous word, a damaged passage); otherwise leave it empty. "notes" at the top level is for anything about the page as a whole; otherwise empty.
- Return JSON only, matching the schema you are given.

Page real-kaskel-to-schnorr-1864. Lines:

l1: 84
l2: Hochgeehrter Freund!
l3: So herrlich und unvergleichlich als
l4: gestern im unsterblichen Werke
l5: Meyerbeer's, habe ich Ihren so
l6: hochtrefflichen Sohn nie gehört,
l7: obwohl er stets der erste Tenor
l8: der Gegenwart ist. Meine
l9: Freude wurde verdoppelt, als
l10: ich seinen so hochverehrten, und
l11: ebenfalls unvergleichlichen Vater
l12: unter den Zuhörern erblickte
l13: und mir sagte was dieser da
l14: empfinden müßte!
l15: Aber meinem verewigten
l16: großen Freunde war, ach! das
l17: Glück nicht beschieden, seinen
l18: Raoul so zu hören!
l19: Gott erhalte Sie!
l20: Ihr treu ergebener
l21: am 30t Juny Carl Kaskel
l22: 1864

segments.translation: Never have I heard your so most excellent son as gloriously and incomparably as yesterday in Meyerbeer's immortal work, although he is always the foremost tenor of the present day. My joy was doubled when I caught sight of his so highly honoured and likewise incomparable father among the listeners, and told myself what he must be feeling there!
segments.note: The sentence-final 'müßte' is as transcribed; the sentence ends with an exclamation mark.

segments.translation: But my departed great friend, alas, was not granted the good fortune of hearing his Raoul sung in this way!
segments.note: 'seinen Raoul' refers to the role of Raoul in Meyerbeer's work; 'meinem verewigten großen Freunde' presumably refers to Meyerbeer.

segments.translation: Your faithfully devoted, on the 30th of June, Carl Kaskel, 1864
segments.note: Closing formula and dateline; the date at the left of the signature is read together with the year on l22.
